findings.title: Shard splitting now interpolates every query twice, and ad-hoc filters may be added twice
findings.body: runShardSplitQuery already calls datasource.applyTemplateVariables (passing request.filters) on every target. Each shard sub-request then goes through runSplitQuery, which now calls applyTemplateVariables again on the same, already-interpolated targets. The backend path then interpolates a third time. The second pass can re-apply ad-hoc filters to an expression that already contains them, which duplicates the filter clauses. It can also re-process interpolated variable values that contain `$` or regex characters. It also wastes work once per shard group and per time chunk. The updated shard test now expects 5 applyTemplateVariables calls instead of 1, which confirms the repeated work. Interpolation should happen once: either skip it in runSplitQuery when the caller has already interpolated, or stop interpolating in runShardSplitQuery.

findings.title: Test asserts an implementation-detail call count that bakes in double interpolation
findings.body: `expect(datasource.applyTemplateVariables).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(5)` ties the test to the exact number of shard groups and sub-requests (1 initial call plus 4 inside runSplitQuery). It breaks whenever grouping changes, and it asserts the redundant double interpolation as expected behaviour. The mock also mutates the passed query in place, unlike the real implementation, which returns a new object, so in-place mutation masks any problem with repeated application.
